Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for scalable quantum error correction; this work identifies a new type of correlated error induced by radiation.
method: Experimental study using a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, measuring error correlations under controlled radiation exposure.
result: Discovered that ionizing radiation produces phase error bursts that are correlated across multiple qubits, persisting even with advanced shielding.
conclusion: These correlated errors undermine standard error correction codes, necessitating new mitigation strategies such as improved shielding or error-correcting codes robust to burst errors.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process due to electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: To understand the heating dynamics and thermalization mechanisms in mesoscopic electron baths at high magnetic fields, which is relevant for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved noise thermometry was used to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: A two-step thermalization process was observed, attributed to the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into energy dissipation and thermalization in mesoscopic systems, with implications for quantum device design and information thermodynamics.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with integrated passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance, protecting qubits from thermal backaction and enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Conventional isolators and circulators are bulky, lossy, and incompatible with large-scale integration, limiting the scalability of superconducting quantum processors. This work aims to eliminate the need for external isolators by incorporating reverse isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier (TWPA) using Josephson junctions, where passive reverse isolation is achieved through directional coupling and phase matching, preventing back-propagating noise from reaching the qubit.
result: The amplifier demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance (added noise close to the standard quantum limit) while providing >20 dB of reverse isolation, effectively protecting qubits from thermal backaction without external isolators.
conclusion: This integrated isolator-free readout architecture simplifies the microwave chain, reduces loss, and is compatible with scalable superconducting quantum processors, potentially improving readout fidelity and system integration.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that random monitoring in quantum error-correcting codes can improve decoding by leveraging measurement outcomes, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication.
motivation: To understand how measurement randomness affects the performance of quantum error-correcting codes, particularly in the context of monitored quantum dynamics and fault tolerance.
method: The authors analyze stabilizer codes under random projective measurements, studying the stability of logical information and the statistics of logical measurements. They use concepts from quantum information theory and statistical mechanics.
result: Random monitoring can enhance decodability by providing additional information about errors, and logical measurement statistics reveal new stability properties under partial measurements.
conclusion: The findings suggest new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication protocols that exploit measurement randomness, opening avenues for practical implementations.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale up quantum security devices by integrating self-testing quantum random number generation on a photonic chip, addressing the need for practical, production-ready quantum cryptography hardware.
method: The authors designed and fabricated a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, leveraging integrated photonic components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness without trusting the devices, achieving high generation rates and demonstrating the feasibility of chip-scale device-independent quantum cryptography.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices, with implications for quantum communication networks and device-independent protocols.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing a more complete picture of the noise environment affecting qubits.
conclusion: This technique enhances qubit noise characterization, which is important for error mitigation and quantum device optimization. It may be applied to various qubit platforms.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade with system size, enabling strong antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: To overcome the need for strong single-emitter coupling in conventional photon blockade, which is experimentally challenging, by leveraging collective effects in an ensemble.
method: Theoretical analysis of an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, using a master equation approach to study photon statistics and transmission.
result: Photon blockade is collectively enhanced, with antibunching improving as the number of emitters increases, and high transmission is maintained.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a scalable route to photon blockade using collective effects, relevant for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics at the few-photon level.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limitations of existing Josephson mixers in terms of bandwidth and saturation power, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: Design and experimental characterization of impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, likely using superconducting circuits and Josephson junctions.
result: Achieved enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to traditional degenerate Josephson mixers, enabling simultaneous amplification and frequency conversion of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These mixers are promising for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in quantum transduction and readout of superconducting qubits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov

Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that are easier to detect and correct.
method: The authors leverage the parity symmetry of integer fluxonium qubits and implement a dispersive readout scheme that maps relaxation events to erasure flags.
result: They demonstrate that energy relaxation errors are converted into erasures with high fidelity, leading to a significant boost in effective coherence times.
conclusion: This erasure conversion technique offers a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing with fluxonium qubits, and future work may extend it to other qubit modalities.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a system that mimics a negative-mass mechanical oscillator to cancel backaction.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing, and may be extended to other hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes mode multiplexing in an optical cavity to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, addressing scalability.
motivation: Cavity-enhanced operations are powerful but typically limited to a single atom or small ensemble; scaling to large arrays is needed for quantum computing and simulation.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian or Laguerre-Gaussian modes) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations with minimal crosstalk, and analyze the trade-offs between number of modes, cavity finesse, and atom-cavity coupling.
conclusion: This work provides a path to scalable cavity-enhanced quantum operations in neutral-atom platforms, with implications for quantum computing, networking, and hybrid systems.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-

tldr: Demonstration of >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: To achieve the high fidelities required for fault-tolerant quantum computing, simultaneous high-fidelity operations across all qubit functionalities are needed.
method: The authors used a superconducting circuit with tunable couplers and developed a new calibration protocol to optimize qubit-coupler interactions and minimize crosstalk.
result: They achieved >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting quantum processors.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, advancing the scalability of superconducting quantum computers and enabling more complex quantum algorithms.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution

abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for long, coherent evolution. This work aims to reduce the simulation overhead by introducing randomization.
method: The authors propose partially randomized product formulas for Hamiltonian simulation, which combine deterministic and random elements to achieve lower error scaling. They analyze the performance in the context of quantum phase estimation.
result: The method yields orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard product formulas, while maintaining the same accuracy.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement for quantum phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices. Future work could explore applications to other quantum algorithms and further optimization of the randomization scheme.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Haar-random quantum codes exhibit a sharp transition between decodable and nondecodable phases under local noise, with a simple mechanism governing the transition.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum communication and computation. This work aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using random matrix theory and statistical physics methods, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix under local noise and identifying the transition point.
result: They find a clear transition between decodable and nondecodable phases, determined by the code rate and noise strength, with the transition being first-order in nature. The spectral properties show universal behavior near the transition.
conclusion: The results provide a simple mechanism for coding transitions in random codes, with implications for designing practical quantum error-correcting codes and understanding fundamental limits of quantum communication.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for quantum information processing in hybrid systems combining continuous-variable (oscillator) and discrete-variable (qudit) degrees of freedom, which are relevant for platforms like superconducting circuits coupled to spin ensembles.
method: The authors generalize the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems using symplectic operations over rings, and construct stabilizer states and codes based on noncommutative geometry.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes are derived, with potential improvements for displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for hybrid quantum processors and error correction, with implications for quantum sensing and communication in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrates that non-Gaussian operations can surpass these limits, enabling colder states.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to near ground state is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental constraints on Gaussian operations limit achievable temperatures. Understanding whether non-Gaussian resources can overcome these limits is key for advancing quantum control.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Gaussian constraints, deriving bounds on cooling performance for Gaussian operations. They then analyze specific non-Gaussian protocols (e.g., photon subtraction, addition) to show enhancements beyond Gaussian limits.
result: Gaussian operations are shown to have a strict cooling bound, while non-Gaussian operations can achieve arbitrarily low temperatures in principle, though with practical trade-offs in success probability or resource overhead.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources provide a pathway to sub-bath cooling, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing. Future work should explore experimental implementations and optimization of non-Gaussian cooling protocols.

method: The authors replace block encoding with local circuits, leveraging a combination of Hamiltonian simulation and dissipative steps to engineer a thermalizing dynamics that converges to the Gibbs state.
result: The protocol achieves rapid mixing and high accuracy for a range of Hamiltonians, with rigorous bounds on the mixing time and error, and is compatible with current quantum hardware constraints.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for Gibbs state preparation on near-term quantum devices, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics simulations.

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.

tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on information storage and transmission in quantum memories under Markovian noise using information-theoretic tools.
motivation: To understand the ultimate capabilities of noisy quantum memories for storing and transmitting quantum information, which is crucial for quantum computing and communication.
method: The authors employ information-theoretic analysis, likely using entropy measures and quantum channel capacities, to derive bounds on storage and transmission rates under Markovian noise.
result: Key findings include tight bounds on the achievable rates for reliable storage and transmission, possibly showing that Markovian noise imposes fundamental constraints that cannot be overcome by any encoding or decoding scheme.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical foundation for designing error-correcting codes and quantum memories, with implications for quantum communication and thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.

tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor, enabling concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and precision of multiparameter estimation in quantum sensing by leveraging entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin.

They create entanglement between the two spins and perform a single measurement sequence to estimate multiple parameters (amplitude, frequency, phase) simultaneously.
result: The entanglement-assisted protocol achieves concurrent estimation of three parameters with precision beyond the standard quantum limit, demonstrating the advantage of entanglement in multiparameter sensing.
conclusion: This work shows the practical utility of entanglement in quantum sensing and opens avenues for more efficient quantum sensors, with potential applications in quantum communication and metrology.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: This review classifies universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum systems using quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal behavior lacks a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to underlying symmetries and topological features.
conclusion: The classification provides a foundation for understanding and engineering nonequilibrium phases, with implications for quantum technologies and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is non-classical and non-quantum, focusing on tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement.
motivation: To address the possibility that gravity may be neither classical nor quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that can constrain such theories.
method: Information-theoretic analysis of thought experiments and review of proposed tabletop-scale experiments for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE).
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified and analyzed, showing how entanglement can be used as a witness for non-classical gravity.
conclusion: These approaches provide a path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity at low energies, with implications for quantum foundations and information thermodynamics.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental demonstration of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs and distribution over 21 km fiber.
motivation: To systematically investigate asymmetric HOM revival interference in QFCs and demonstrate efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals, which had not been reported.
method: Experimental setup with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz QFCs, HOM interference measurements over multiple time-bins, and distribution through 21 km optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: Observed HOM revivals up to 20 time-bins with visibilities around 70%, and distributed QFC over 21 km fiber with 12 time-bins and 70.5% visibility; deviation attributed to residual frequency distinguishability.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing, including high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for exponential fast-forwarding of Lindbladian dynamics and uses them to achieve exponential improvement in estimating Gibbs state properties under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Fast-forwarding of dissipative dynamics (Lindbladians) is largely unexplored, and estimating Gibbs state properties is crucial for quantum many-body physics and thermodynamics. The authors aim to overcome the no fast-forwarding theorem for Lindbladians and improve efficiency of Gibbs property estimation.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For structured jump operators (block-diagonal Paulis), they modify the algorithm to achieve exponential fast-forwarding in circuit depth while preserving query complexity via parallel access. They then apply these techniques to estimate Gibbs state properties using quantum singular value transformation.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties when the input state satisfies certain coherence conditions (e.g., being a pure state). This improvement is applied to ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. The level of improvement depends on the coherence resource in the input state.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that exponential fast-forwarding is possible for certain Lindbladian dynamics, leading to significant speedups for Gibbs property estimation. This opens avenues for efficient quantum algorithms in thermodynamics and quantum information, with potential applications in quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics.

title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled Pure States Of Multipartite Quantum Systems
authors: Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Rafał Bistroń, Albert Rico, Arul Lakshminarayan And Karol Życzkowski
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states of a system composed of N parties are distinguished by the property that for any splitting at least one partial trace is maximally mixed. Due to maximal possible correlations between any two selected subsystems these states have numerous applications in various fields of quantum information processing including multi-user teleportation, quantum error correction and secret sharing. We present an updated survey of various techniques to generate such strongly entangled states, including those going beyond the standard construction of graph and stabilizer states. Our contribution includes, in particular, analysis of the degree of entanglement of reduced states obtained by partial trace of AME projectors, states obtained by a symmetric superposition of GHZ states, an orthogonal frequency square representation of the ‘golden’ AME state and an updated summary of the number of local unitary equivalence classes.
tldr: This paper surveys absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, their constructions, and applications in quantum information tasks like teleportation and secret sharing.
motivation: AME states are crucial for many quantum protocols, but their existence and construction for arbitrary numbers of parties remain challenging; this work aims to provide an updated overview of known methods and new constructions.
method: The authors review graph and stabilizer state constructions, introduce symmetric superpositions of GHZ states, use orthogonal frequency squares to represent the golden AME state, and analyze local unitary equivalence classes.
result: They present new families of AME states, including those beyond stabilizer states, and characterize the entanglement of reduced states from AME projectors.
conclusion: The findings expand the toolkit for generating AME states, which can benefit quantum error correction, secret sharing, and multiparty communication protocols.

title: A Quantum Kinetic Theory Of Photon Bose–Einstein Condensation In Semiconductors
authors: José L Figueiredo, Ross C Schofield, Ming Fu, Robert A Nyman, Rupert Oulton, Hugo Terças And Florian Mintert
abstract: Photon condensation in semiconductor microcavities is a transformative technique for engineering quantum states of light at room temperature by tailoring strong but incoherent light-matter interactions. While continuous-wave and electrical pumping offer exceptional prospects for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies, harnessing these requires conceptual advances in understanding non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors. We resolve this challenge through an ab initio quantum kinetic theory capturing how Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering mediate photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductors. Our microscopic model shows that at high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier–carrier Coulomb scattering, in clear contrast to the rovibrational relaxation that governs dye-based photon condensates. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, Bose-condensed, multimode, and lasing phases, quantitatively in agreement with recent experiments. Crucially, we identify how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources. This work thus provides the foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices operating beyond conventional laser paradigms.
tldr: This paper develops a quantum kinetic theory for photon Bose-Einstein condensation in semiconductors, revealing that carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering dominates thermalization at high densities, and predicts a nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, condensed, multimode, and lasing phases.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors for engineering quantum states of light at room temperature, which is crucial for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies.
method: Ab initio quantum kinetic theory incorporating Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering, modeling photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductor microcavities.
result: At high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering, contrasting with dye-based condensates. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram and shows how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes.
conclusion: Provides a foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices operating beyond conventional laser paradigms, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources.

title: Profile Of John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, And John M. Martinis: 2025 Nobel Laureates In Physics
authors: Andrew N. Clelandsteven M. Girvinapritzker School Of Molecular Engineering, University Of Chicago, Chicago IL 60637bdepartment Of Physics, Yale University, New Haven CT 06520
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 22, June 2026.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics jointly to John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis for their foundational discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in ...
tldr: The paper profiles the 2025 Nobel laureates in Physics for their foundational work on macroscopic quantum tunneling and energy quantization in superconducting circuits, which underpins modern quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To recognize and summarize the groundbreaking contributions of John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis that led to the Nobel Prize, highlighting their impact on quantum physics and technology.
method: The paper is a biographical and scientific profile, likely reviewing key experiments and theoretical insights by the laureates, such as the demonstration of macroscopic quantum tunneling in Josephson junctions and the development of superconducting qubits.
result: The laureates established the reality of macroscopic quantum phenomena, enabling the development of superconducting qubits and quantum circuits, which are central to quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: Their work has paved the way for quantum technologies, including quantum computing and hybrid systems combining superconducting circuits with other quantum systems, with ongoing implications for quantum communication and thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Dual-band Atomic Mirror Based On Subwavelength Atomic Arrays Under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, and Yan Zhang

Subwavelength atomic arrays offer a powerful platform for engineering cooperative light-matter interactions and enabling quantum metasurfaces. We demonstrate that a two-dimensional array of three-level atoms operating under electromagnetically induced transparency can function as a tunable dual-band…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063705] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A 2D array of three-level atoms under EIT acts as a tunable dual-band mirror with high reflectivity and narrow linewidths.
motivation: To engineer a tunable, dual-band atomic mirror using subwavelength atomic arrays for quantum metasurface applications.
method: Theoretical analysis of a 2D array of three-level Λ-type atoms with EIT, using coupled-dipole equations and transfer-matrix methods to compute reflectivity and transmission.
result: The array exhibits two high-reflectivity bands corresponding to the two EIT transparency windows, with tunability via control field parameters and atomic density.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for multi-band quantum metasurfaces and may enable applications in quantum information processing and light-matter interfaces.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery to integrate two QEC codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is essential for universal quantum computing but typically requires resource-intensive distillation protocols. This work aims to reduce overhead.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to combine two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling teleportation of non-Clifford gates without distillation.
result: The scheme achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with reduced resource overhead compared to traditional distillation methods.
conclusion: The approach simplifies universal gate set implementation and may improve efficiency in fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Boltzmann Sampling By Diabatic Quantum Annealing
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Yongjoo Baek
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Yongjoo Baek

Boltzmann sampling is a central component of many computational frameworks, including numerous algorithms in machine learning. Although quantum annealers have been investigated as potential fast Boltzmann samplers, their dependence on environmental noise makes precise control of the effective temper…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a diabatic quantum annealing protocol for Boltzmann sampling that enables precise control of effective temperature without relying on environmental noise.
motivation: Quantum annealers are promising for fast Boltzmann sampling, but their dependence on environmental noise makes precise temperature control difficult. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors introduce a diabatic quantum annealing protocol that uses controlled non-adiabatic transitions to mimic thermal distributions at a desired temperature, bypassing the need for noise-based thermalization.
result: The protocol achieves accurate Boltzmann sampling with tunable effective temperature, demonstrated through numerical simulations on small spin systems.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach for using quantum annealers as programmable Boltzmann samplers, with potential applications in machine learning and optimization.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for understanding qubit leakage and improving readout in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can ionize, escaping their computational states into highly excited states, which degrades performance. Understanding this process is essential for developing better readout schemes and error mitigation.
method: The authors experimentally probe transmon ionization using microwave spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements, analyzing multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions that lead to ionization and characterize the dynamics of these transitions, revealing how qubits escape to high-energy states.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transmon leakage mechanisms, guiding the design of improved readout and control protocols to suppress ionization in quantum processors.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
motivation: To accurately capture complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon quantum processors, which are critical for reliable simulation and algorithm performance.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that accounts for correlated errors across multiple qubits and over time, and validate it using a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used as a proxy simulator.
conclusion: This work provides a practical noise modeling framework that enhances the fidelity of quantum simulations on transmon processors, with implications for error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes via code surgery, enabling efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation without additional code blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement of logical qubits is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require extra resources or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that allows simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while preserving the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves high-performance parallel measurements without needing additional code blocks, maintaining key code properties essential for quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations, with implications for quantum memory and computation architectures.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A synthetic time-domain photonic processor achieves universal linear transformations with exponentially reduced hardware complexity, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: To overcome hardware scalability challenges in photonic quantum computing by reducing the number of physical components needed for universal linear transformations.
method: The authors propose a synthetic time dimension approach where optical modes are encoded in time bins, and operations are performed using a single tunable coupler and delay lines, achieving all-to-all connectivity.
result: The processor demonstrates exponential reduction in hardware resources while maintaining high fidelity and exceeding performance thresholds for universal quantum computation under realistic noise.
conclusion: This work paves the way for scalable photonic quantum processors and may impact quantum communication networks by enabling efficient linear optical transformations.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond key distribution, addressing the growing need for diverse quantum-enhanced security tasks.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum money, commitments, oblivious transfer) and discusses experimental implementations using photonic systems.
result: It categorizes quantum crypto primitives, explains their security definitions and limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental progress.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers many functionalities beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; future work should focus on improving security proofs and experimental scalability.

title: Acoustic Bound Pair States In The Continuum Induced By Off-Site Two-Body Interactions
authors: Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, and Zhengyou Liu

A novel many-body bound state in the continuum induced entirely by uniform off-site 2-body interactions is observed by mapping a quantum 1D Bose-Hubbard model onto a 2D macroscopic phononic crystal.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226501] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Observation of many-body bound states in the continuum induced by uniform off-site two-body interactions, realized by mapping a 1D Bose-Hubbard model onto a 2D phononic crystal.
motivation: To demonstrate a novel type of bound state in the continuum (BIC) that arises solely from off-site interactions, which has not been previously observed and could have implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.
method: The authors map a quantum 1D Bose-Hubbard model with off-site two-body interactions onto a classical 2D macroscopic phononic crystal, using acoustic waves to simulate the quantum system and observe bound states.
result: They experimentally observe acoustic bound pair states in the continuum induced by uniform off-site interactions, confirming the theoretical prediction.
conclusion: This work provides a classical analog of a quantum many-body BIC, offering a platform to study interaction-induced bound states and potentially extending to other quantum systems.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions
authors: Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, And Jörg Kröger
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, and Jörg Kröger

A new experiment shows that spin-polarized currents conducted by helical organic molecules are not just a measurement artifact, as some researchers suspected.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226201] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Experiments demonstrate that helical organic molecules can act as spin polarizers in superconducting junctions, confirming that the observed spin-polarized currents are not artifacts.
motivation: There was controversy whether spin-polarized currents through helical organic molecules are genuine or measurement artifacts. This work aims to settle the debate.
method: The authors performed experiments with superconducting junctions incorporating helical organic molecules and measured spin-polarized currents.
result: They observed clear spin polarization, ruling out artifact explanations and establishing the molecules as effective spin polarizers.
conclusion: The findings validate the use of helical molecules for spin injection in superconducting spintronics and open avenues for hybrid quantum systems combining organic molecules with superconductors.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria under detection loophole conditions, finding that PPT remains more robust.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies but is hindered by experimental imperfections like detection inefficiency. The study aims to understand how the detection loophole affects two major detection methods.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the detection efficiency thresholds for PPT and moment-based criteria, likely using numerical simulations or analytical bounds for specific quantum states.
result: The PPT criterion can detect entanglement with lower detection efficiency than moment-based criteria, meaning it is more robust against the detection loophole.
conclusion: The findings guide experimentalists in choosing entanglement detection methods under realistic conditions, and suggest further study of other loopholes and multi-partite scenarios.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in digital-analog quantum computing, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians as entangling resources.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a promising paradigm that combines the flexibility of digital gates with the efficiency of analog interactions, but systematic methods for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians are needed.
method: The authors derive explicit formulas for decomposing target Hamiltonians into sequences of single-qubit gates and the system's natural interaction Hamiltonian, using Trotterization and analytical error bounds.
result: They provide closed-form expressions for the required digital-analog sequences and demonstrate their efficiency for common interaction Hamiltonians, showing reduced gate counts compared to purely digital approaches.
conclusion: The work provides a practical toolkit for implementing Hamiltonian simulation on digital-analog platforms, with implications for quantum chemistry and optimization, and suggests future extensions to error mitigation and larger systems.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines the super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial-order spin interactions.
motivation: To develop a protocol that suppresses noise from spin interactions, which is crucial for quantum state protection and quantum gyroscope applications.
method: The authors introduce a protocol that uses the quantum super-Zeno effect (frequent projective measurements) on spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from polynomial-order spin interactions.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations; for spin-1/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved protection.
conclusion: The protocol offers a new way to protect quantum states from certain types of noise, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, achieving fast and high-fidelity quantum operations.
motivation: To exploit the larger Hilbert space of qudits for more efficient quantum information processing, and to demonstrate control on a molecular spin platform.
method: The authors use optimal control theory (GRAPE algorithm) to design microwave pulses that implement single-qudit gates on the GdW30 molecule, characterized by its spin-7/2 ground state.
result: They achieve time-optimal pulses for a set of universal gates with fidelities above 99.9% and gate times on the order of tens of nanoseconds.
conclusion: Molecular spin qudits are a promising platform for quantum computing, and optimal control can mitigate decoherence by minimizing gate times.

title: Spin Entanglement Of Two Atoms Through Coupling To Their Thermal Motion
authors: Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, And Stuart S. Szigeti
abstract:
Author(s): Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, and Stuart S. Szigeti

The spin dynamics of two alkali-metal atoms in an optical tweezer is driven by spin-changing collisions that couple the spin state of the atoms to their relative motion. This paper experimentally studies the resulting spin states when the relative motion is in a thermal state with [MATH] much la…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062201] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates spin entanglement between two atoms mediated by their thermal relative motion via spin-changing collisions in an optical tweezer.
motivation: To understand how thermal motion, typically a source of decoherence, can be harnessed to generate entanglement between atomic spins.
method: Two alkali-metal atoms are trapped in an optical tweezer, and spin-changing collisions couple their spin states to their relative motional state, which is initially thermal. The resulting spin entanglement is characterized via state tomography.
result: The experiment shows that significant spin entanglement can be generated even when the motional state is thermal, with the degree of entanglement depending on the temperature and interaction parameters.
conclusion: Thermal motion can be a resource for entanglement generation, offering a new mechanism for creating entangled states in atomic systems without requiring ground-state cooling.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional derivatives, revealing violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium thermodynamics in systems with long-range interactions and fractional dynamics, particularly how phase coexistence deviates from local equilibrium assumptions.
method: Numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, which modify the density of states at low wave numbers.
result: The model exhibits first-order phase transitions where local equilibrium thermodynamics is violated, indicating that standard thermodynamic relations do not hold in this fractional system.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for generalized thermodynamic frameworks for systems with fractional dynamics and long-range interactions, with implications for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
